messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: High tail latency detected for dedicated-pool-us-east-phi (p99 > 4s) - auto-escalating to #incidents :rotating_light:
ani: paging oncall. seeing client alerts + increased error rate on streaming endpoints. reading dashboards now.
marcus: I see a sharp jump around 12:42 UTC. p95 from 300ms -> 1.1s, p99 spiking to ~4.8s. queue depth jumped to ~420.
sophie: streaming stalls reported by several customers (stream chunk timeout). logs show long warmup latency on newly allocated GPUs ~70-120s.
devon: autoscaler added nodes at 12:41 but handshake/agent-heartbeat delay prevented traffic until warmup finished. autoscaler metrics: requested 6 -> allocated 6 -> ready only after 90s.
jordan: looks like handshake RTT between control-plane and private nodes timed out intermittently (TLS handshake retries). investigating network traces.
ani: customer impact? any 5xx spikes?
marcus: yes - spikes in 502/504 for streaming proxied requests, roughly 1.8k errors in 10m window. top-affected customers: acme (20% of calls degrade), fluxlabs (10%).
ops-bot: Current mitigations applied: 
- routed 35% of traffic to hosted-fallback cluster (non-dedicated)
- enabled prefix-KV cache for frequent prefixes
- increased queue cap from 200 -> 600 for the affected route (temporary) :gear:
ani: routing helped reduce tail latency on non-dedicated by ~600ms but hosted capacity is also near its burst limit.
samir: suggest immediate manual cold-start optimization: pin a smaller quantized model variant for high-throughput endpoints to reduce warmup time. can flip in 2-3min.
sophie: also propose lowering per-instance max-concurrency during warmup to avoid giant cold-cache queues (reduce to 4).
marcus: agreed. implementing model-variant fallback now.
ani: logging our live customer-facing status: "Experiencing increased latency and streaming stalls for some Dedicated customers in US-EAST. Team has routed traffic to fallback clusters and is manually scaling/optimizing warmup. Oncall will continue mitigation and runbook steps."
jordan: network traces show sporadic TLS handshake timeouts between control plane and some VPCs starting 12:40 - likely the cause of delayed ready signals. I'm opening a ticket with infra-networking.
devon: pace of autoscaler handshake: normal expected handshake < 5s. observed 40-70s on 4 nodes. kernel logs show repeated retransmits from control-plane agent.
marcus: quick mitigation checklist I'm doing now:
```
1) reroute 25-50% traffic to hosted cluster
2) flip model fallback for heavy routes -> fast-quantized variant
3) reduce instance concurrency during warmup
4) raise autoscaler min for this pool (temp) to keep warm nodes warm
5) drain slow nodes gradually
```
sophie: adding step: temporarily extend request frontend timeout to reduce 504s while we warm up nodes.
ani: I'm drafting a Slack status update for affected customers and paging support. Samir please coordinate docs note if we need to communicate SLO impact.
samir: will draft customer note. initial SLO calc: p99 target was 2s; we hit 4.8s at peak. Estimated breach window ~ 12:40 - 13:05 UTC.
jordan: infra-networking says they're seeing BGP flaps to a subset of racks - investigating. could be packet loss causing handshake retries.
devon: manual scale-up applied: increased min-replicas for pool to 4 (was 1). also toggled faster warmup path on runtime which skips cache priming for first N requests.
marcus: after toggles, p99 dropped to ~1.9s in 6 minutes, queue depth down to 90. streaming stall error rate dropped by 80%. charts improving. great. :thumbsup:
ani: open action items (owner, ETA):
- infra-networking to resolve handshake flaps (jordan, 4h)
- autoscaler: add handshake/backoff telemetry + alert (devon, 2d)
- runtime: optimize warmup fast-path and allow config hotflip (sophie, 3d)
- support: customer comms + postmortem (samir, 1d)
- product: evaluate routing policies to prefer hot-hosts for high-SLO customers (marcus, 1w)

jordan: I'm escalating the network ticket to infra oncall. linking packet captures + timestamps.
ops-bot: NOTE: temporary hosted routing will incur cross-cluster egress charges; finance aware (FYI).
ani: any remaining impact? please call out if you see any lingering 5xx or streaming stalls.
samir: support: currently monitoring top 10 customers, a few small tail errors ~still ~50 errors last 10m but trending down.
devon: logging for postmortem: 
```
- p95 timeline
- p99 timeline
- autoscaler handshake times for each allocation
- network packet loss / TLS retries
- warmup durations per model variant
- traffic reroute events
```
marcus: will capture dashboards and attach to PM.
ani: thanks team. I'll run the handoff to next oncall in 30m with the mitigation checklist. keeping incident open until network flaps cleared and p99 stable under 2s for 30m. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATED: Mitigations applied, incident under monitoring.
